voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyaya 44: Vasuki, distressed, asks his sister whether the sage left her with child, for the serpents' sake; she answers that he said 'asti', 'it is there', and that he never spoke falsely even in jest. Vasuki rejoices and honours her. In time she bears a boy, radiant like a child of the gods, who grows up in Vasuki's house; he studies the Vedas and their branches with Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu; he keeps the vows of a celibate student, and grows, the hope of the serpents. (Shaunaka, Sauti's listener, is himself of Bhrigu's line: 1.4–5.) The cliffhanger turns to Hastinapura, where Janamejaya asks his ministers how his father died (1.45).
structure: From episode 21: COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, ≤ 3 s; opening chosen by content (not a fixed rotation): a question card by content: the small boy in a ring of serpents' eyes, the card low in the dark below him) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band over its first shot → turn at 40–60 % after one ≈ 0.9 s rest → the cliffhanger image + line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image that dissolves into frame 1. strings.recapLine: "Asti. There is one." And the sage was gone.

lines.text: Can one boy save a whole people?
lines.say: Can one boy [p:40] save a whole people?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a question card by content): the small boy standing in the dark hall inside a vast ring of serpents' eyes that open one by one from frame 1; the card low in the dark beneath him.

lines.text: Vasuki came to his sister at night, afraid for his people.
lines.say: Vasuki came to his sister at night, [p:80] afraid for his people.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): the chamber at night (episode 35's, the lamp lower): Vasuki's hood leans in at the doorway; she sits alone.

lines.speaker: vasuki
lines.say: Did he leave you [p:40] with child?
lines.note: STORY 1 (Vasuki speaks): close on Vasuki's single hood, low, the ruby jewel catching the lamp.

lines.speaker: nagini
lines.text: "He said, there is one. He never spoke a lie."
lines.say: He said, [p:80] there is one. [p:250] He never spoke a lie.
lines.note: STORY 2 (the bride speaks): she lifts her face to her brother; the small gold flame at her waist glows (episode 35's).

lines.text: Vasuki rejoiced, and honoured his sister.
lines.say: Vasuki rejoiced, [p:100] and honoured his sister.
lines.note: STORY 2b: Vasuki bows his great hood to her; the lamplight warms; jewels brought by serpents glint around her.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: All the serpents had left was one unborn child.
lines.say: All the serpents had left [p:80] was one unborn child.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti, a twenty-fourth angle: from beside the elder, Sauti seen across the fire, his hands cupped as if around a flame).

lines.text: And in time a boy was born, bright as a child of the gods.
lines.say: And in time [p:60] a boy was born, [p:120] bright as a child of the gods.
lines.note: STORY 3 · THE TURN (≈ 40 %): after the 0.9 s silence, NEW LIGHT, the birth: the hall floods with white-gold light from a newborn held in his mother's arms; the serpents' heads bow in rings.
STORY 4: Vasuki lifts his hood over mother and child like a canopy; plaque "Astika".

lines.text: He grew like the waxing moon, and kept every vow.
lines.say: He grew like the waxing moon, [p:100] and kept every vow.
lines.note: STORY 6: NEW LIGHT, the night sky over the serpent world: the moon waxes through four phases on the beats while the boy, seen in silhouette on a rock, grows taller in each.

lines.text: And the serpents watched him, and remembered the promise.
lines.say: And the serpents watched him, [p:100] and remembered the promise.
lines.note: STORY 7: the hall at dawn (episode 35's light): the boy walks through the rows of serpents, who turn as he passes; Elapatra among them.

lines.text: He learned the sacred texts from the sage Chyavana.
lines.say: He learned the sacred texts [p:80] from the sage Chyavana.
lines.note: STORY 5: NEW LIGHT, Bhrigu's line's hermitage at morning (green forest, a sacred fire of ember-red): the boy seated before the ember-lit teacher; palm-leaf pages; plaque "Chyavana".

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Shaunaka, that teacher was of your own family.
lines.say: Shaunaka, [p:100] that teacher was of your own family.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti, a twenty-fifth angle: the reverse: Sauti turning to look straight at him across the fire; the elder's face lit by surprise).

lines.text: Meanwhile, in Hastinapura, a king was asking how his father died.
lines.say: Meanwhile, [p:100] in Hastinapura, [p:100] a king was asking how his father died.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger, the catalog line): NEW LIGHT, Janamejaya's court at night by torchlight: the young king on his throne leaning forward, his ministers before him; behind him a painted panel of his father.
